cleanIntro:
This guide follows PTR Industries' 9mm Owner's Manual, which covers the PTR 9C, 9CT, 9KT and 9R and never names the 9CTMP, so check your variant against it. Every step below is quoted from that book and stated as generally as the book states it.

PTR's own field strip for its 9mm roller-delayed blowback guns, in PTR's order and no further. One takedown pin holds the gun together; behind it the end cap and recoil spring come off as one unit, the trigger group drops out by the pistol grip, and the bolt carrier slides out the back. PTR takes the bolt group apart one stage further and then stops, referring everything past that to a gunsmith.

steps.title: Know what you are holding
steps.action: This guide follows PTR Industries' 9mm Owner's Manual, which covers the PTR 9C, 9CT, 9KT and 9R and never names the 9CTMP, so check your variant against it. Every step below is quoted from that book and stated as generally as the book states it.
steps.prose: PTR prints one book for its 9mm roller-delayed guns and says plainly on its first page that the text, pictures and exploded views do not necessarily show every variation. If a part on your gun does not match what a step describes, stop and contact PTR rather than forcing it.
steps.quote: This manual address the PTR “Models: 9C; 9CT; 9KT; and 9R” products.
steps.cite: PTR 9mm Owner's Manual (Models 9C, 9CT, 9KT and 9R) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — PTR 9mm Owner's Manual — statement of the models covered, p.3

steps.title: Selector on SAFE, magazine out
steps.action: Point the muzzle in a safe direction. Put the safety selector lever on S (SAFE), then press the magazine release at the back of the magazine well on the right side and take the magazine out by pulling it down while rotating its rear toward the front of the gun.
steps.prose: The magazine rocks out the way it rocked in — front first, rear rolled up into place on the way in, so on the way out PTR has you rotate the rear toward the front as you pull it down.
steps.quote: safety selector lever in the “S” or “SAFE” position and then depress the magazine release located at
steps.cite: PTR 9mm Owner's Manual (Models 9C, 9CT, 9KT and 9R) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Use of Your Firearm, step 4, p.9

steps.title: Cocking handle back and locked up in its notch
steps.action: Muzzle still in a safe direction, unfold the cocking handle on the left side at the front of the handguard, pull it toward you (rearward), and rotate it up into the retaining notch near the rear of the cocking tube. The bolt is now held open.
steps.prose: The cocking handle on this gun folds and lives at the front of the handguard, not at the receiver. It only holds the bolt open when it is rotated up into its notch at the back of the tube — let go of it short of the notch and the bolt runs home.
steps.quote: of the handguard and pull the cocking handle towards you (rearward); then rotate the handle upward into the retaining
steps.cite: PTR 9mm Owner's Manual (Models 9C, 9CT, 9KT and 9R) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 2, p.7

steps.title: Chamber inspected; bolt let forward and the trigger dropped
steps.action: Look into the chamber and confirm it is clear. Then pull the cocking handle slightly rearward, rotate it down out of the notch and let it ride forward. Still pointing the muzzle in a safe direction, rotate the selector to F (FIRE) and press the trigger so the bolt returns to its closed, fired position. Rotate the selector back to S (SAFE) before going on.
steps.prose: PTR has you strip this gun with the bolt closed and the hammer down, which is why the trigger press is part of clearing rather than an afterthought. Do it only after you have seen an empty chamber, and put the selector back on SAFE straight away.
steps.quote: “F” or “FIRE” and depress the trigger to allow the bolt to return to its closed or
steps.cite: PTR 9mm Owner's Manual (Models 9C, 9CT, 9KT and 9R) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 2, p.7

steps.title: Slings, scopes and mounts off
steps.action: With the gun checked unloaded, take off any sling, scope and scope mount before you start.
steps.prose: PTR puts this in its first disassembly step, right after the unloaded check, and puts them back on as the last step of reassembly.
steps.cite: PTR 9mm Owner's Manual (Models 9C, 9CT, 9KT and 9R) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 1, p.7

steps.title: The one takedown pin out, right to left
steps.action: Push out the single takedown pin just forward of the end cap, from the right side of the gun to the left. PTR says no tools should be needed.
steps.prose: If the pin will not move by hand, check that you are pushing from the right — the book gives the direction, and the pin goes back in the opposite way, left to right.
steps.quote: Remove the one takedown pin located just
steps.cite: PTR 9mm Owner's Manual (Models 9C, 9CT, 9KT and 9R) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 3, p.7

steps.title: End cap and recoil spring assembly straight back
steps.action: Pull the end cap straight back to the rear. The end cap and the recoil spring assembly come off together as one unit.
steps.prose: Straight back is the instruction — the recoil spring assembly is attached to the end cap and slides out of the receiver with it, so there is nothing to hold or catch.
steps.quote: will come off as one unit.
steps.cite: PTR 9mm Owner's Manual (Models 9C, 9CT, 9KT and 9R) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 4, p.7

steps.title: Trigger group down by the pistol grip
steps.action: With the end cap off, pull down on the pistol grip and the whole trigger group comes away from the receiver.
steps.prose: The trigger group hinges off at the front, where it hooks over the rear of the magazine well. It goes back the same way: front first, then the rear rolled up.
steps.quote: can now remove the entire trigger group by pulling downward on the pistol grip.
steps.cite: PTR 9mm Owner's Manual (Models 9C, 9CT, 9KT and 9R) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 5, p.7

steps.title: Bolt carrier out the rear of the receiver
steps.action: Tip the muzzle upward, unfold the cocking handle and pull it rearward. The bolt carrier should slide easily out of the rear of the receiver.
steps.prose: PTR's word is easily. If the carrier does not slide out, check that the end cap and the trigger group are both off before doing anything more.
steps.cite: PTR 9mm Owner's Manual (Models 9C, 9CT, 9KT and 9R) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 6, p.7

steps.title: Bolt head a half turn and forward off the carrier
steps.action: Turn the bolt head one half turn counterclockwise and pull it forward off the bolt carrier.
steps.prose: Half a turn, counterclockwise, then forward. The locking rollers and their retainer are part of the bolt head in PTR's parts list and come off with it.
steps.cite: PTR 9mm Owner's Manual (Models 9C, 9CT, 9KT and 9R) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 7, p.7

steps.title: Locking piece, firing pin and spring out of the carrier
steps.action: Push in on the locking piece and slowly rotate it counterclockwise until its lug clears the bolt carrier. Then take the locking piece, the firing pin and the firing pin spring out of the carrier.
steps.prose: The firing pin spring sits behind the locking piece, which is why PTR says push in and rotate slowly rather than just turn it.
steps.quote: Then push in and slowly rotate
steps.cite: PTR 9mm Owner's Manual (Models 9C, 9CT, 9KT and 9R) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 7, p.7

steps.title: Bore and chamber
steps.action: PTR leaves cleaning method and kit to you. The one bore method it prints, in its break-in procedure, is a solvent-wet cotton patch pushed through the bore, then a solvent-wet bronze brush stroked through five to ten times, another wet patch, and dry patches until no solvent or wetness is left in the barrel.
steps.prose: The barrel and chamber are the parts PTR wants left DRY after cleaning — the dry patches at the end are not optional.
steps.quote: push a cotton patch, wet with solvent through the
steps.cite: PTR 9mm Owner's Manual (Models 9C, 9CT, 9KT and 9R) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Cleaning and Break In — break-in procedure, step I, p.4

steps.title: Bolt group, trunnion and barrel face
steps.action: Clean the internal components PTR names: the bolt head, the bolt carrier, the trunnion, the barrel face and the locking piece.
steps.prose: These are the parts PTR names when it has you clean the gun before measuring bolt gap, and the bolt gap is what the rollers and locking piece set. Carbon left on the bolt face or the barrel face changes that measurement.
steps.cite: PTR 9mm Owner's Manual (Models 9C, 9CT, 9KT and 9R) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Bolt Gap Specification, Measurement and Maintenance, step III, p.5

steps.title: Oil the internals lightly; barrel and chamber stay dry
steps.action: After cleaning and before firing, lightly oil the internal parts — the bolt head, the bolt carrier and the locking piece — and keep the barrel and the chamber dry.
steps.prose: A wet chamber is the mistake this line exists to prevent. Oil goes on the moving internals and nowhere in the bore.
steps.quote: carrier, locking piece), while keeping the barrel and
steps.cite: PTR 9mm Owner's Manual (Models 9C, 9CT, 9KT and 9R) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Cleaning and Break In, p.4

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You have the receiver with the barrel and handguard still fitted, the takedown pin, the end cap with its recoil spring assembly, the trigger group, the bolt carrier, the bolt head, the locking piece, the firing pin and the firing pin spring. That is all of PTR's disassembly.
steps.prose: PTR's own line ends the strip here: no further disassembly is either necessary or recommended, and anything that needs more goes to a qualified gunsmith.
steps.quote: recommended beyond this point. Any repair or maintenance procedure that requires further disassembly of the weapon should be referred to a qualified gunsmith.
steps.cite: PTR 9mm Owner's Manual (Models 9C, 9CT, 9KT and 9R) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 7, p.7

deepAbsentReason: The book ends at the field strip: its disassembly procedure stops once the bolt group is apart (step 7, p.7), states that no further disassembly is necessary or recommended, and refers anything further to a qualified gunsmith. It publishes no deeper procedure.

cleaning.name: BORE AND CHAMBER
tasks: Solvent-wet cotton patch pushed through the bore
Solvent-wet bronze brush, five to ten strokes
Another wet patch, then dry patches until no solvent or wetness is left

cleaning.name: BOLT GROUP AND TRUNNION
tasks: Bolt head and its locking rollers

cleaning.name: OIL
tasks: Light oil on the bolt head, bolt carrier and locking piece
Do not oil the barrel or the chamber

reassembly: Firing pin, firing pin spring and locking piece back into the bolt carrier; press the locking piece in and turn it counterclockwise until it locks. PTR's reassembly page shows the clock positions — follow it.

Bolt head onto the locking piece with the flat top of the bolt head at the top, so the roller pin engages the slot in the locking piece; turn the bolt head slightly counterclockwise until the angled relief cut at its base lines up with the carrier. The bolt head should then slide forward and back along the locking piece.

Cocking handle in its forward-most position. Complete bolt carrier assembly into the rear of the receiver as far as it will go, then point the muzzle at the ground and it seats itself into the trunnion.
Trigger group back on: front of the group over the rear of the magazine well first, then roll the rear, with the pistol grip, up into position.
End cap and recoil spring assembly slid back over the rear of the receiver, with the recoil spring seated in its recess in the bolt carrier.
Takedown pin into the end cap hole from the left side to the right side of the receiver.
Slings, scopes and scope mounts back on.
fncheck: PTR prints no function check for these guns. Before the first shot, confirm the gun is clear and the barrel is free of obstruction: the book's safety rules say "Be sure that your barrel is clear of any obstructions prior to firing."
